key_insight: PWLNet makes neural process surrogates optimization-compatible through exact and piecewise-linear embeddings, with compact models enabling tractable decisions.
engineering_relevance: Engineers can embed learned steady-state and dynamic process models in Pyomo optimization workflows to improve operating policies.
method: Combine baseline or physics-informed training with optimization-aware pruning.
Embed ReLU, exact tanh, or PWL-tanh networks using MILP, nonlinear, or binary-free SOSX formulations.
Use PWL-native training to match training and embedded activations, avoiding extra linearization error.
evidence_signal: Across four benchmarks, reported results include a 6.5× MILP speedup after 15% pruning on Williams–Otto and a 4% true-plant economic gain over the best ramp-and-hold policy on Van de Vusse.
watch_item: Constraint fidelity remains a concern: the hydroformylation exact-tanh controller reached 20.002 bar against a 20-bar limit, and longer horizons or physics-informed training did not consistently improve closed-loop results.
paper_title: PWLNet: A Framework for Linearized Neural Surrogates in Nonlinear Process Optimization
